title: 02 Systems of Linear Equations and RREF: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 02 Systems of Linear Equations and RREF — five interactive visuals taking one system from its augmented matrix, through elimination to REF and RREF, and on to rank, dependence and singularity.

1. Columns To Equations | The bridge from lesson 01: two sliders set the weights on the columns of A, and the SVG draws the tip-to-tail combination reaching (or missing) the target b, while each row is scored as its own equation and the augmented matrix [A|b] is shown alongside | Solving is matrix-vector multiplication run backwards — b is given and the weights are unknown; a row IS an equation, a column IS one variable's coefficients, and the constants ride in the last column so elimination cannot leave them behind.

2. Row Operations Sandbox | Apply the three elementary row operations by hand to the augmented matrix of x+2y-z=2, 2x+3y+z=9, x-y+2z=5 (or press Run to REF / Run to RREF), watching a live operation log while two pills show that x=(2,1,2) still satisfies every row and that rank never moves; scaling by k=0 and self-swaps are refused with an explanation | The three moves are legal precisely because each is reversible, so they re-describe a system rather than change it — which is why Gaussian elimination is an algorithm with a stopping condition and runs identically by hand or in code.

3. Echelon Two Ways | Toggle one matrix between REF and RREF to see the single extra requirement (zeros above each pivot, pivots scaled to 1) appear, then drag the free variable x3 = t and watch x1 = 3+2t, x2 = 1-4t slide while both equations keep holding | RREF states the answer instead of implying it, exposing rank, free variables and consistency at a glance; a free variable is free, not zero, so reporting one triple names a single point on an infinite solution line.

4. Rank And Dependence | Pick one of three vector sets and hunt with the c1, c2, c3 sliders for a combination with weights not all zero that reaches the zero vector, while a live rank pill reports whether the vectors span a line, a plane, or all of R^3 | Dependence is the existence of that non-trivial witness, and rank counts it before you look: rank below the number of vectors guarantees a witness exists, rank equal to it guarantees none does — and rank counts independent rows and independent columns alike.

5. Singular Or Not | Two dials on x+2y=4 and m·x+4y=c: dragging the coefficient m to 2 collapses the eliminated bottom row to zeros and makes the matrix singular, after which the constant c alone decides between infinitely many solutions and none, with both lines drawn live | Singularity is a statement about the coefficient structure alone — rank(A) never moves as c is dragged end to end — while the constant on a zero row is what separates a merely redundant system from a contradictory one.
